plain_english: Now the fifteenth chapter: the Lord said the imperishable asvattha has its root above and branches below; its leaves are the vedic meters, and whoever knows it is a knower of the veda.
sanskrit_cite: atha pañcadaśo'dhyāyaḥ   śrībhagavānuvāca   ūrdhvamūlamadhaḥ śākhamaśvatthaṃ prāhuravyayam | chandāṃsi  yasya parṇāni yastaṃ veda sa vedavit | anena śāstrāntareṣu yaducyate-aśvatthaḥ sarvaṃ sa  evopāsanīyaḥ-ityādi tasya bhagavadbhahyopāsā tātparyamityucyate | mūlaṃpraśāntaṃ rūpam | tat ūrdhvaṃ-sarvato hi nivṛttasya  tadāptiḥ | chandāṃsi parṇānīti-yathā vṛkṣasya  mānatvaphalavattvasarasatādayaḥ parṇaiḥ sūcyante evaṃ  brahmatattvasya vedopalakṣitaśāstradvārikā pratītirityākhyāyate

plain_english: Its branches spread up and down, grown by the strands and bearing sense-objects as shoots; below, roots extend, bound to action, in the human world.
sanskrit_cite: adhaścordhvaṃ prasṛtā yasya śākhā guṇapravṛddhā  viṣayapravālāḥ | adhaśca mūlānyanusantatāni karmānubandhīni  manuṣyaloke

plain_english: Its form is not perceived here thus; it has no end, no beginning, no stable foundation; this deeply rooted asvattha must be cut with the sharpened weapon of non-attachment.
sanskrit_cite: na rūpamasyeha tathopalabhyate nānto na cādirna ca sampratiṣṭhā | aśvatthamenaṃ suvirūḍhamūla- masaṅgaśastreṇa śitena cchittvā

plain_english: Then that state is to be sought, to which having gone one does not return again; I take refuge in that very first person, from whom the ancient emanation has spread.
sanskrit_cite: tataḥ padaṃ tatparimārgitavyaṃ yasmingato na nivarteta bhūyaḥ | tameva cādyaṃ puruṣaṃ prapadye- dyataḥ pravṛttiḥ prasṛtā  purāṇī

plain_english: The unconfused, free from pride and delusion, go to the imperishable state; its actions, rooted below, are to be cut, and that tranquil imperishable state alone is the goal.
sanskrit_cite: nirmānamohā jitasaṅgadoṣā adhyātmanityā vinivṛttakāmāḥ | dvandvairvimuktāḥ sukhaduḥkhasaṃjñai- rgacchantyamūḍhāḥ  padamavyayaṃ tat | guṇaiḥ-sattvādibhiḥ | pravṛddhāḥ-devādisthāvarāntatayā | tasya ca śubhāśubhātmakāni karmāṇi aghastanamūlāni | taṃ  chittveti-viśeṣye kriyābhidhīyamānā sāmarthyādatra  viśeṣaṇapadamupādatte daṇḍī praiṣyānanubrūyāt-iti vidhivat | tenādhorūḍhāni mūlānyasya cchindyāditi | tat-padaṃ-praśāntam  avyayaṃ padaṃ tadeva

plain_english: Neither sun nor moon nor fire illumines it; having gone there one does not return; that supreme abode of mine is beyond the limitation of space, time, and instruments.
sanskrit_cite: na tadbhāsayate sūryo na śaśāṅko na pāvakaḥ | yadgatvā na  nivartante taddhāma paramaṃ mama | sūryādīnāṃ tatrānavakāśaḥ | teṣāṃ kālādyavacchedāt  vedyatvāt karaṇopakārakatvāt | tasya tu dikkālādyanavacchedāt  vedakatvāt karaṇapravartakatvāt-tadatītatvāt

plain_english: The eternal living being draws mind and senses in the living world; its portionhood of Brahman is figurative, not a real division.
sanskrit_cite: mamaivāṃśo jīvaloke jīvabhūtaḥ sanātanaḥ | manaḥ  ṣaṣṭhānīndriyāṇi prakṛtisthāni karṣati | brahmaṇa evāyamaṃśa iti | ajñānadharmatayā  paripūrṇasyāsaṃvedanāñcetanatānivṛtteścāṃśatvamupacaritaṃ  na punarvastuto'ṃśavattopapadyate-   pradeśo'pi brahmaṇaḥ sārvarūpyamanatikrāntaḥ | (avikalpyaśca)   iti hi śrutiḥ | eṣaiva caupacārikatā yathāvasaraṃ yojanīyeti na  vipratipattavyam

plain_english: The lord obtains and leaves bodies, carrying the subtle instruments with him, as wind carries scent from place to place.
sanskrit_cite: śarīraṃ yadavāpnoti yaccāpyutkrāmatīśvaraḥ | gṛhītvaitāni  saṃyati vāyurgandhānivāśayāt | avāpnoti-gṛhṇāti | utkrāmati-tyajati | etaiḥ saha | yathā vāyuḥ  sarvagato viśrāntidhāma pārthivaṃ prāpya tato gandhamānīya  sthānāntare tatsahita eva saṃkrāmati evaṃ jīvaḥ puryaṣṭakena  saha | evaṃ sṛṣṭau saṃhāre caitaiḥ sāhityamasyoktvā sthitāvapi  sthānāsanamananādirūpāyāṃ viṣayagrahaṇātmikāyāṃ  tatsahitasyaivāsya vyāpāra iti niścīyate

plain_english: Presiding over ear, eye, touch, taste, smell, and mind, this self enjoys the objects.
sanskrit_cite: śrotraṃ cakṣuḥ sparśanaṃ ca rasanaṃ ghrāṇameva ca | adhiṣṭhāya manaścāyaṃ viṣayānupasevate

plain_english: The deluded do not see the self standing, departing, or enjoying; the awakened see its knowing form everywhere.
sanskrit_cite: tiṣṭhantamutkrāmantaṃ vā bhuñjānaṃ vā guṇānvitam | vimūḍhā  nānupaśyanti paśyanti jñānacakṣuṣaḥ | mana ityanenāntaḥkaraṇamupalakṣyate | ata eva  śarīrasthitiyogāttiṣṭhantam | śarīrāntaragrahaṇāya  utkrāmantam | viṣayānvā bhuñjānaṃ mūḍhā na  paśyanti-aprabuddhatvāt | prabuddhāstu sarvatraiva  bodharūpamevānusandadhānā jānantyeva  ityalupta-samādhayaḥ-teṣāṃ yatnaparatvāt

plain_english: Striving yogis see the self established in the self, but unperfected selves do not; effort alone does not yield fullness.
sanskrit_cite: yatanto yoginaścainaṃ paśyantyātmanyavasthitam | yatanto'pyakṛtātmāno nainaṃ paśyantyacetasaḥ | akṛtātmanāṃ tu yatno'pi na phalāya-aparipakvakaṣāyatvāt | nahi  śaradi salilādisāmagrīsaṃmarde'pi dhānyabījāni upyamānāni  phalasaṃpade'lam | ata eva sāmagrī eva sāsya na bhavati-anyadeva  kila madhumāsasaṃbhṛtajaladharapaṭalīpreritamambhaḥ | kācideva ca  sā bhūḥ yasyāṃ śiśiravivaśīkṛtāyāṃ ravikarasparśenaiva  kāntiḥ | evamakṛtātmanāṃ yatno na  sakalāṅgaparipūrṇatvamāyāti | eta eva prāpyāpyupāyaṃ  pārameśvaradīkṣādi ye  tathāvidhakrodhamohādigranthisandarbhagarbhīkṛtāntardṛśaḥ  teṣūpāya eva sākalyaṃ na bhajatīti mantavyam | yaduktaṃ-   krodhādau dṛśyabhāve hi dīkṣito'pi na muktibhāk | iti

plain_english: Know the light residing in sun, moon, and fire, which illuminates the whole world, to be mine.
sanskrit_cite: yadādityagataṃ tejo jagadbhāsayate'khilam | yaccandramasi yaccāgnau  tattejo viddhi māmakam

plain_english: Entering the earth, I sustain beings by my energy and nourish all herbs, having become the moon, the essence of sap.
sanskrit_cite: gāmāviśya ca bhūtāni dhārayāmyahamojasā | puṣṇāmi  cauṣadhīḥ sarvāḥ somo bhūtvā rasātmakaḥ

plain_english: I become the universal fire, abiding in the bodies of living beings, joined with prāṇa and apāna, and cook the fourfold food. The venerable teachers say that the world-sustaining power of the five elements, as whole and part, is the Lord's māheśvarya. The sun's light illuminates and sustains; the moon's light illuminates and nourishes herbs; fire's light illuminates, dries, burns, sweats, and cooks; and space is all-pervading as awareness-space. Therefore, having stated the knowable form, he shows the self as supreme Lord, all-knowing, independent, and all-maker.
sanskrit_cite: ahaṃ vaiśvānaro bhūtvā prāṇināṃ dehamāsthitaḥ | prāṇāpānasamāyuktaḥ pacāmyannaṃ caturvidham | arkāditejasrayarūpatayā  daśamādhyāyasūcitasṛṣṭisthitisaṃhāraprakaṭīkaraṇe  śrīguravaḥ prāhuḥ-bhūtapañcakasya samastavyastatayā  yallokadhārakatvaṃ tadbhagavata eva māheśvaryamityetadanena | tathāhi | ravitejasaḥ prakāśakatvaṃ dhārakatvaṃ  ca-tejodharādvayatādātmyāt | tadetaduktaṃ-yadādityagatam iti  gāmāviśya ca iti cārdhadvayena | cāndraṃ tejaḥ prakāśakaṃ  poṣakaṃ ca-jalatejoyogāt | taduktaṃ-yaccandramasi ityanena bhāgena   puṣṇāmi cauṣadhīḥ sarvāḥ somo bhūtvā rasātmakaḥ | iti cārdhaślokena | vāhnaṃ tu tejaḥ  prakāśanaśoṣaṇadahanasvedanapacanātmakaṃ-pṛthivyaptejovāyuyogā  t | tadetadihoktaṃ-yaccāgnau ityanena ahaṃ vaiśvānaraḥ-ityanena ca | nabhastu bodhāvakāśarūpatayā sarvagatameva | ata eva bodhyarūpatāmuktvā  tadbodhyasvarūpapṛṣṭhapatitasvātantryabodhasvabhāvamātmānaṃ  parasvabhāvaṃ parameśvararūpaṃ sarvajñānasvatantraṃ  sarvakartāraṃ darśayitumāha-

plain_english: I dwell in the heart of all; from me come memory, knowledge, and removal. I alone am known by all the Vedas and Vedanta. The knowable nature is independent knowing, and the reflection 'there I am' is knowledge as new manifestation and world-creation. Conceptual knowledge is removal, bond-creation, and maya-made fixation; remembering is the residue of withdrawn impressions manifesting again. Thus all knowledges are withdrawn, and agency as freedom preceded by omniscience is declared. All scriptures determine the supreme Lord-principle alone; the Lord's freedom is world-agency through creating, uprooting, and re-establishing own nature. Others, by difference-cognition, make removal and thereby produce Vedanta and Veda through self-realization.
sanskrit_cite: sarvasya cāhaṃ hṛdi sanniviṣṭo mattaḥ smṛtirjñānamapohanaṃ ca | vedaiśca sarvairahameva vedyo vedāntakṛtadvedavideva cāham | sarvasya vedyasya yat hṛt-samastāharaṇasvatantrabodhasvabhāvaṃ  tatrāhamiti yo vimarśastata evāpūrvābhāsanāmayaṃ jñānaṃ  viśvamahāsṛṣṭirūpam | ayaṃ ghaṭa eva-iti  sarvātmakabhāvakhaṇḍanāsāraṃ vikalpajñānātmakamapohanaṃ  pāśavasṛṣṭirūpamāyāmayapramātrucitam | smaraṇaṃ ca  saṃskāraśeṣatāṃ nītasya saṃhṛtasya punaravabhāsanātmakamiti  iyatā samastajñānāni saṃhṛtāni | iti sarvajñatāpūrvakaṃ  svātantryarūpaṃ kartṛtvamuktam | sarvairiti-saṃbhūya kila  sarvaśāstrāṇāṃ parameśatattvameva nirūpyam | vedavedāntakartṛtvena karmaphalatatsaṃbandhādidvāratayā  aśeṣaviśvanirmāṇe tadunmūlanena punaḥ svarūpapratiṣṭhāpane  bhagavata eva svātantryamiti viśvakartṛtvamuktam | anye tu  apohanam-anenākṛtenedaṃ bhavati iti vyatirekabuddhiḥ | vedāntaṃ  karoti ityātmasādbhāvena | evaṃ vedam

plain_english: In the world there are two persons: the perishable and the imperishable. The perishable is all beings, while the immutable is called imperishable.
sanskrit_cite: dvāvimau puruṣau loke kṣaraścākṣara eva ca | kṣaraḥ sarvāṇi  bhūtāni kūṭastho'kṣara ucyate

plain_english: Another highest person, called the supreme self, enters the three worlds and sustains the imperishable Lord.
sanskrit_cite: uttamaḥ puruṣastvanyaḥ paramātmetyudāhṛtaḥ | yo  lokatrayamāviśya bibhartyavyaya īśvaraḥ

plain_english: Because I transcend both the perishable and the imperishable, I am supreme; therefore I am renowned in the world and in the Veda as the supreme person. The text says there are these two persons in the world. Even in an unawakened state, people know the conscious self with a body made of elements as perishable form, and from the world's delusion the dualistic view does not cease. But I, all-gracious, split the dualistic knot and, pervading all the world, am to be known. I transcend the perishable because beings are inert, and the imperishable because all-pervasion is denied in the unawakened self. Thus, by explanations beginning with the supreme person in world and Veda, he alone is said to be the supreme nondual self.
sanskrit_cite: yasmātkṣaramatīto'hamakṣarādapi cottamaḥ | ato'smi loke vede ca  prathitaḥ puruṣottamaḥ | loke dvāvimau puruṣau-iti granthenedamucyate-loke  tāvadaprabuddhasvabhāvo'pi sarva  pṛthivyādibhūtārabdhaśarīramātmānaṃ cetanaṃ kṣararūpaṃ  jānātīti lokasya mūḍhatvāt dvaitadhīrna nivartate | ahaṃ tu  sakalānugrāhī dvaitagranthiṃ vibhidya sakalalokavyāpakatayā vedya  iti | kṣaramatītaḥ-bhūtānāṃ jaḍatvāt | akṣaramatītaḥ-ātmano'prabuddhatve sarvavyāpakatvakhaṇḍanāt | puruṣottamo loke vede'pi sa uttamaḥ puruṣaḥ-ityādibhirvyākyaiḥ  sa eva paramātmādvaya evamucyate

plain_english: One who knows the supreme person without delusion worships with all being; all forms, actions, and knowledge are recognized as the Lord.
sanskrit_cite: yo māmevamasammūḍho jānāti puruṣottamam | sa sarvavidbhajati māṃ  sarvabhāvena bhārata | evaṃ jānānaḥ sarvamayaṃ māmeva brahmatattvamupāsīnaḥ sarvaṃ  manmayatvena vidan sarveṇa bhāvena-mūrtikriyājñānātmakena māmeva  bhajate | yatpaśyati tadbhagavanmūrtitaye-tyādi | tathā ca mayaiva  śivaśaktyavinābhāvastotre-   tava ca kācana na stutirambike sakalaśabdamayī kila te tanuḥ | nikhilamūrtiṣu me bhavadanvayo manasijāsu bahiṣprasarāsu ca | iti vicintya śive śamitāśive jagati jātamayatravaśādidam | stutijapārcanacintanavarjitā na khalu kācana kālakalāpi me | iti

plain_english: This most secret scripture is completed by understanding nondual recognition; accomplishment comes from knowing, not from action, and the goal is absorption in the Lord.
sanskrit_cite: iti guhyatamaṃ śāstramidamuktaṃ mayānagha | etadbuddhvā  buddhimānsyātkṛtakṛtyaśca bhārata | guhyatamaṃ-sarvādvayapratipādakatvāt | etadeva buddhā  buddhimattvaṃ natu vyavahārabuddhā | etena ca jñātenaiva  kṛtakṛtyatā natu kṛtenāpi  śatruvijayārthāharaṇastryupabhogādinā | cakāro'dbhutadyotakaḥ | kṛtena hi kṛtakṛtyatā dṛṣṭā etena tu jñātenaiveti citram | itiśabdena śāstrasya samāptiḥ sūcitā-vaktavyasya paripūrṇatayā  samāptatvāt | tathāhi | ṣoḍaśādhyāyena śiṣyasyārjunasya  kevalaṃ yogyatā pratipādyate | natūpadiśyate kiṃcit | daivī  hyevaṃvidhā saṃpat āsurī cāvidyāmayyetādṛśī saṃpat | tvaṃ  ca vidyāmayīṃ daivīṃ saṃpadaṃmabhiprāptaḥ-ityetāvati hi  tātparyam | yadvakṣyati mā śucaḥ saṃpadaṃ daivīm-iti | ata eva  pūrvaṃ vidyāvidyāsaṃghaṭṭanirūpaṇāvasare  devāsurasaṃgrāmacchalena vidyāvidyayoḥ saṃgharṣa iti sūcitam | evaṃ ca śiṣyasvarūpe prādhānyena nirūpyamāṇe  prasaṅgato'nyadapyuktam | ityadhyāyadvayaṃ bhaviṣyati | upadeśastvita eva parisamāptaḥ | sarvabhāvena hi  parameśvarabhajanamāveśarūpaṃ prāpyam | tadarthaṃ  cātyatsarvamityuktaṃ prāk | sarvamāheśvarasvarūpāveśa eva hi  paramaṃ śivamiti śivam

plain_english: Having removed great duality-delusion and made consciousness Brahman-filled, the sage always enters it even in worldly practice.
sanskrit_cite: atra saṃgrahaślokaḥ   hṛtvā dvaitamahāmohaṃ kṛtvā brahmamayīṃ citim | laukike  vyavahāre'pi munirnityaṃ samāviśet | iti śrīmahāmaheśvarācāryavaryarājānakābhinavaguptapādaviracite  śrīmadbhagavadgītārthasaṃgrahe pañcadaśo'dhyāyaḥ
